action_items: LOW-priority (React warning, not a functional bug): WinClaimModal calls requireLogin?.() inside the render body when open && !user. This triggers a React dev warning: 'Cannot update a component (Home) while rendering a different component (WinClaimModal). To locate the bad setState() call inside Home...'. Behaviour still works (login modal opens, win modal closes), but this should be moved to a useEffect: e.g. useEffect(() => { if (open && !user) { requireLogin?.(); } }, [open, user, requireLogin]); and return null while !user.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py claim_win correctly enforces the full validation chain: auth -> ctype in (played,posted,live) -> file present -> Gemini extract_win_slip -> status=='won' -> legs>=2 -> anti-duplicate sig -> live-branch (legs>=4 & every odds>1.60) or matched>=3 for played/posted -> played legs>=5, credits capped at WIN_MAX_CREDITS(20). All error paths return proper HTTP codes (400/401/409/422).

build_systems() emits exactly 5 systems as required, each _finalize_system with distinct key/title/subtitle/risk. Sicherheits-Kombi uses 4x 'Über 0.5 Tore' legs (~1.08 each) giving total_odds=1.36 — well inside the 1.2-1.7 target. Real bookmaker odds are applied to safe/bankers/vals via _apply_real; smartvalue reuses the 'vals' list which is fine and matches the requirement.
hall_of_fame() properly hides mongo _id, sig, user_id fields via projection and sorts by total_odds desc, limit=24 — matches 'Best of' sort spec.

React setState-in-render in WinClaimModal.jsx line 25-28: calling requireLogin?.() during render triggers a Home setState. Not a bug in user flow but produces a console error and could cause double-invocation in StrictMode/concurrent mode. Move to useEffect.

App.js hero-earn-btn onClick={() => setWinOpen(true)} unconditionally — the auth gate is delegated to WinClaimModal which is fine architecturally, but the setState-in-render issue above stems from this. Preferable to compute requireLogin inline at click time.
HallOfFame.jsx correctly renders empty state via data-testid=hof-empty, and passes onEarn up to Home which reuses the same WinClaimModal. Good composability.
